headline: Results cool from a tough prior-year comparison
summary_short: Net revenue fell 9.2% y/y to $1,839M and net bookings dropped 13% against a tough prior-year comparison from College Football 25; diluted EPS of $0.54 was down 51.4% y/y as GAAP operating margin compressed to 10.9% from 19.0%.
summary_long: Revenue was $1,839M, down 9.2% y/y and up 10.0% q/q; net bookings fell 13% y/y, mainly reflecting last year's extraordinary College Football 25 launch, though Madden NFL 26 and Apex Legends returned to bookings growth. GAAP operating income fell to $200M (10.9% margin, from 19.0%) as R&D spend rose to $686M; net income was $137M and diluted EPS $0.54, both down roughly 51-53% y/y. Non-GAAP operating margin was 21.8% versus 31.5% a year ago. Operating cash flow was $130M; cash fell to $1,148M after $375M of buybacks and $48M of dividends. EA suspended its earnings call and withdrew forward guidance given the pending $55B take-private deal with PIF, Silver Lake, and Affinity Partners.

GAAP operating income fell as R&D spend rose to $686M from $648M y/y while revenue declined 9.2%, compressing operating margin to 10.9% from 19.0%.
Cash fell as EA funded $375M of buybacks and $48M of dividends largely from a lighter $130M of operating cash flow this quarter, versus $234M a year earlier.
